case: Section 9 Relief — Post-Tribunal-Constitution Maintainability
headline: Section 9 Application Does Not Automatically Become Infructuous Once the Tribunal Is Constituted
summary: The Delhi High Court clarified that a Section 9 application pending before a court does not automatically lapse the moment the arbitral tribunal is constituted; the efficacy proviso under Section 9(3) requires a case-specific assessment of whether the tribunal remains an equally effective forum for the relief sought, rather than a blanket transfer of jurisdiction.

case: Arbitration and Conciliation Bill, 2024 — Legislative Watch
headline: Constitution Bench in Gayatri Balasamy Urges Expedited Passage of Arbitration & Conciliation Bill 2024
summary: The five-judge bench in Gayatri Balasamy explicitly urged the Ministry of Law & Justice to expedite passage of the pending Arbitration and Conciliation Bill, 2024. The Bill proposes key amendments including mandatory timelines for arbitrator appointments, expanded institutional arbitration framework, provisions for emergency arbitrators, and updated enforcement procedures for foreign awards.

case: Recall of Jurisdictional Finding in a Commercial Courts Act Appeal
headline: Calcutta HC Recalls Its Own Jurisdictional Finding After a Binding Supreme Court Precedent Went Unconsidered
summary: A Division Bench of the Calcutta High Court recalled an earlier finding — that a decree was a nullity for want of jurisdiction of the trial judge under the Commercial Courts Act, 2015 — on discovering that a binding Supreme Court precedent bearing directly on the point had escaped consideration when the original order was passed.

case: Commercial Courts Act — 2026 Procedural Amendments
headline: Wider Summary-Judgment Powers and Mandatory E-Filing Take Hold in Commercial Litigation
summary: 2026 has seen Commercial Courts extend summary judgment procedure under Order XIII-A CPC to a broader range of commercial disputes, enabling early disposal without full trial, alongside statutory recognition of e-filing, virtual hearings and electronic evidence protocols as the default mode of practice rather than the exception.

case: Lotus Ventures Joint Development Group
headline: A Joint Venture Partner Cannot Unilaterally Change the Agreed Profit-Sharing Formula Mid-Project
summary: The Calcutta High Court restrained a joint venture partner from unilaterally altering the profit-sharing formula recorded in the parties' joint venture agreement, holding that a JV agreement is a binding commercial contract like any other, and that one partner's unilateral departure from its agreed terms, however commercially justified it may claim the change to be, amounts to a breach actionable by the other partner

case: Verification Standard for Related-Party Claims in CIRP
headline: Resolution Professional Must Independently Verify Related-Party Claims, Not Rely on the Corporate Debtor's Own Books
summary: NCLAT reiterated that a claim filed by an entity connected to the corporate debtor cannot be admitted merely on the strength of the corporate debtor's own internal ledger entries. A resolution professional's verification duty under the CIRP Regulations is heightened, not diminished, where the claimant is a related party, given the direct bearing claim composition has on CoC voting.

case: Essel Infraprojects — NCLT Order Set Aside for Reliance on AI-Hallucinated Precedents
headline: Supreme Court Sets Aside NCLT Insolvency Order Built on Fabricated, AI-Generated Case Law
summary: The Supreme Court set aside an NCLT order in the Essel Infraprojects insolvency matter after discovering the tribunal's reasoning relied on non-existent precedents generated by an AI tool, and directed the Bar Council of India to frame norms governing the verification of AI-assisted legal research before it is placed before courts and tribunals.

case: Public Interest Litigation on Bank-ARC Settlements — Notice Issued to Centre & RBI
headline: SC Flags Nexus Between Banks, ARCs and Borrowers Over Steep Haircut Settlements
summary: A bench led by the Chief Justice raised concern over a plea alleging that ₹1,537 crore owed to public sector banks was settled through two asset reconstruction companies for just ₹73.50 crore, and issued notice to the Centre, the RBI, and other respondents. The Court emphasised it was concerned specifically with the mis-utilisation of public money, while noting its limited institutional role in second-guessing the co

case: In re: Delays in NCLT Resolution Plan Approvals — AVJ Developers Matter
headline: SC Flags Nearly Two-Year NCLT Delay in Approving Resolution Plans, Seeks Nationwide Data
summary: Hearing a matter arising from the insolvency of AVJ Developers (India) Pvt. Ltd., the Supreme Court expressed serious concern that approval of a resolution plan had remained pending before the NCLT for nearly two years, undermining the Code's time-bound design. The Court directed that nationwide data on pending resolution plan approvals be compiled and placed before it.

case: Homebuyer IBC Matters — Multiple Petitions
headline: RERA Is Primary Forum for Homebuyers; IBC Should Not Be Used as a Recovery Tool
summary: In multiple homebuyer IBC matters, the Supreme Court emphasised that RERA is the primary forum for homebuyers' grievances. The IBC should be invoked only for the revival of viable real estate projects — not as a debt recovery mechanism. The Court issued detailed directions: fill NCLT/NCLAT vacancies on priority, create dedicated IBC benches, and form a high-level committee for systemic real estate sector reform.

case: IBC Statutory Timelines — Multiple Matters
headline: IBC's Statutory Timelines Are Mandatory, Not Directory — Strict Compliance Required
summary: Across multiple 2025 rulings, the Supreme Court consistently held that the IBC's statutory timelines — including the 330-day maximum CIRP period under Section 12 — are mandatory and not merely directory. The legislature's intent to create a time-bound framework cannot be diluted by granting ad hoc extensions without a statutory basis.

case: IBBI Circular on CIRP Progress Report Filing Format
headline: IBBI Revises the CIRP Progress-Report Format, Adding a Dedicated Related-Party Transaction Disclosure Field
summary: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India has revised the periodic CIRP progress-report format that resolution professionals must file, introducing a dedicated field requiring specific disclosure of related-party transactions identified during the reporting period, separate from the general transaction-audit summary.

case: Cross-Border Insolvency Framework — Draft Rules
headline: Ministry of Corporate Affairs Circulates Draft Rules for a UNCITRAL Model Law-Based Cross-Border Insolvency Chapter
summary: The Ministry of Corporate Affairs has circulated draft rules for stakeholder comment that would operationalise a cross-border insolvency framework based on the UNCITRAL Model Law, covering recognition of foreign proceedings and cooperation between Indian and foreign courts; the framework remains at the consultation stage and is not yet in force.

case: Pre-Packaged Insolvency Resolution Process — MSME Threshold
headline: IBBI Revises the Default Threshold for MSME Pre-Packaged Insolvency Resolution Process Eligibility
summary: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India has notified a revised minimum default threshold governing which MSME corporate debtors may access the Pre-Packaged Insolvency Resolution Process (PPIRP), extending the route to a wider band of MSME defaults than previously eligible.

case: NCLAT Practice Directions — Paperbook and E-Filing
headline: NCLAT Issues Updated Practice Directions Tightening Paperbook and Certified-Copy Requirements for IBC Appeals
summary: The National Company Law Appellate Tribunal has issued updated practice directions clarifying paperbook formatting and certified-copy submission requirements for appeals filed under Section 61 of the IBC, following a series of decisions treating defective filings as incompetent rather than merely curable.

case: CIRP Regulations — Regulation 35A Amendment
headline: IBBI Amends Regulation 35A to Require Resolution Professionals to Separately Categorise Related-Party Transactions in the Transaction Audit
summary: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India has amended Regulation 35A of the CIRP Regulations to require resolution professionals to separately identify and categorise related-party transactions within the mandatory transaction audit report submitted to the adjudicating authority, rather than folding them into the general avoidance-transaction review.

case: Fast Track CIRP — Eligibility Notification
headline: IBBI Extends Fast-Track CIRP Eligibility to a Wider Band of Unlisted Companies
summary: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India has notified an extension of the asset and turnover thresholds governing eligibility for fast-track Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process under Section 55 of the IBC, bringing a wider band of unlisted companies within the 90-day compressed timeline.

case: Authorised Representative Fee — Homebuyer Class Representation
headline: IBBI Revises the Fee Structure Payable to an Authorised Representative Representing a Class of Homebuyer Creditors
summary: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India has revised the fee structure payable to an Authorised Representative appointed to represent a class of allottee/homebuyer financial creditors in a real estate corporate debtor's CIRP, adjusting the per-meeting and per-class components of the fee.

case: Treatment of Statutory Dues in Approved Resolution Plans
headline: CBDT Issues Clarification on Computing the Liquidation-Value Floor for Statutory Income-Tax Dues in a Resolution Plan
summary: The Central Board of Direct Taxes has issued an internal clarification for field formations on computing the minimum amount statutory income-tax dues must receive under an approved resolution plan, consistent with the Section 53 liquidation-value floor applicable to operational creditors.

case: IPA Inspection Circular — CIRP Compliance Checklist
headline: Leading Insolvency Professional Agency Issues a Standardised Compliance Checklist for Periodic Inspection of Insolvency Professionals
summary: A registered Insolvency Professional Agency has issued a standardised compliance checklist for use in its periodic inspection of enrolled insolvency professionals, covering progress-report timeliness, claims-verification documentation and conflict-of-interest disclosures.

case: Voluntary Liquidation Process Regulations — Timeline Amendment
headline: IBBI Amends Voluntary Liquidation Process Regulations to Tighten Reporting Timelines for Solvent-Company Liquidations
summary: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India has amended the Voluntary Liquidation Process Regulations to tighten the timelines within which a liquidator of a solvent company must file preliminary and final reports, aligning them more closely with the compressed timelines applicable elsewhere under the IBC.

case: NCLT's Jurisdiction Under Section 60(5)(c) IBC — Trademark Ownership Dispute
headline: NCLT Has No Power to Decide Trademark Ownership Disputes Without a Direct Insolvency Link
summary: The Supreme Court held that the National Company Law Tribunal cannot exercise jurisdiction under Section 60(5)(c) of the IBC to adjudicate trademark ownership disputes that lack a direct connection to the corporate debtor's insolvency proceedings, reaffirming that the NCLT's residuary jurisdiction is not a substitute for dedicated IP forums.

case: Swami Ramdev Personality Rights — AI Deepfake John Doe Order
headline: John Doe Order Restrains AI-Generated Deepfakes and Fake Endorsements of Public Figures
summary: The Delhi High Court passed a John Doe order restraining unidentified persons from misusing Swami Ramdev's name, image, voice, and likeness through AI-generated deepfakes, fake endorsements, and unauthorised commercial listings. This is a landmark extension of personality rights jurisprudence to AI-generated content, establishing a template for restraining synthetic media misuse.

case: CRI Guidelines 2025 — Computer-Related Inventions
headline: CGPDTM Notifies Revised Guidelines for Examination of Computer-Related Inventions 2025
summary: The Controller General of Patents, Designs & Trademarks notified final 2025 Guidelines for Examination of Computer-Related Inventions (CRI), clarifying the distinction between patentable technical innovations and non-patentable computer programs 'as such' under Section 3(k) of the Patents Act, 1970. The guidelines align with recent judicial decisions on the 'technical effect' requirement.

case: Kolhapuri Chappal PIL — GI Mark Protection
headline: PIL Filed Alleging Prada Appropriated GI-Protected Kolhapuri Chappal Design
summary: IP advocates filed a PIL in the Bombay High Court alleging that Prada's 2026 Milan collection featured footwear substantially similar to the Kolhapuri chappal — a traditional Indian sandal with an active Geographical Indication registration. The PIL sought injunctions, compensation, and a public apology, arguing that unauthorised commercial appropriation harms Indian artisans.

case: Copyright Act Section 15(2) — Design–Copyright Interface
headline: Copyright Protection Ceases for Artistic Works Industrially Reproduced More Than 50 Times
summary: The Supreme Court laid down a twin test: copyright protection for an artistic work ceases under Section 15(2) of the Copyright Act when the work is (a) registrable as a design under the Designs Act, 2000, (b) has not been registered under that Act, and (c) has been industrially reproduced more than 50 times. Once all three conditions are met, the work falls outside copyright into the Designs Act domain.

case: Aventis LLC — Contempt Proceedings (Decided Feb 3, 2025)
headline: ₹5 Lakh Fine + Imprisonment for Wilful Violation of Injunction in ALLEGRA Trademark Case
summary: The Bombay High Court held Healing Pharma and DM Pharma in contempt for violating a prior injunction protecting Aventis LLC's ALLEGRA antihistamine trademark. The defendants had been marketing 'ALLERGEGRA' on near-identical packaging. The Court imposed a ₹5 lakh fine with four weeks' imprisonment in case of non-payment.

case: Form 27 Working Statement Compliance — Enforcement Notice
headline: Patent Office Flags Non-Filing of Form 27 Working Statements, Signals Closer Scrutiny of Compulsory Licensing Grounds
summary: The Patent Office issued a compliance notice reminding patentees of their obligation under Section 146 of the Patents Act to file Form 27 statements on the working of a patented invention in India, noting that a pattern of non-filing or a patent remaining unworked can form part of the evidentiary basis for a future compulsory licence application under Section 84.

case: Registration Practice Note — SICLD Act Layout-Design Applications
headline: Registry Issues Practice Note on Documentary Requirements for Semiconductor Layout-Design Registration
summary: The Registry administering the Semiconductor Integrated Circuits Layout-Design Act, 2000 issued a practice note clarifying the documentary evidence required to establish originality of a layout-design at the time of filing, including design-history records and evidence that the layout was not commercially exploited more than two years prior to the application.

case: M&A Practice Advisory — IP Ownership Gaps
headline: Practitioners Flag Recurring IP Ownership Gaps Surfacing in Business Acquisition Due Diligence
summary: Legal and transaction advisory commentary has highlighted a recurring pattern in mid-market acquisitions: target companies' core trademarks or software copyrights registered in a founder's personal name rather than the company's, and missing or incomplete invention-assignment clauses in early employment contracts, both of which require corrective assignment and recordation before a deal can safely close.

case: Registration Practice Note — Works Involving AI-Assisted Tools
headline: Copyright Office Practice Note Addresses Applications Disclosing AI-Assisted Authorship
summary: Responding to a rise in copyright applications involving works created with AI-assisted tools, the Copyright Office issued a practice note reiterating that the Copyright Act, 1957 requires a human author for copyrightable subject matter, and that applicants must accurately disclose the extent of any AI tool's contribution to a submitted work at the time of filing.

case: Higher Pension Under EPS-95 — Implementation Guidance
headline: Employees' Pension Scheme — Higher Pension Option
summary: EPFO has issued further implementation guidance clarifying the documentation and employer-contribution reconciliation process for members who opted for higher pension under EPS-95, following the earlier Supreme Court ruling permitting the option.

case: Proposal to Revise ESI Wage Ceiling Under Review
headline: Employees' State Insurance — Wage Ceiling Revision
summary: The Ministry of Labour and Employment has signalled that a revision of the wage ceiling for mandatory ESI coverage is under review, which would bring a larger band of employees within the scheme's mandatory ambit if notified.

case: POSH Act Annual Report Filing Deadline Reiterated
court: Ministry of Women & Child Development / Labour Ministry
headline: POSH Act — Annual Compliance Reporting
summary: Authorities have reiterated the requirement for employers to file their annual POSH Internal Committee report, including the number of complaints received and resolved, within the prescribed timeline, with continuing emphasis on enforcement against non-filing.

case: State ICC Registration Portal for Internal Committees Goes Live
headline: POSH Act — Online Internal Committee Registration Portal
summary: A state labour department has launched an online portal requiring employers within the state to register the composition and contact details of each Internal Committee constituted under Section 4, alongside the existing annual reporting obligation to the District Officer.

case: Clarification on External Member Honorarium and Engagement Terms
headline: POSH Act — Guidance on External Member Engagement
summary: The Ministry has issued clarificatory guidance on the engagement of external members under Section 4(2)(c), addressing permissible honorarium arrangements and reiterating that an external member's engagement must not create a financial dependency on the employer that could compromise independence during an inquiry.

case: Model ICC Training Curriculum Circulated to States
headline: POSH Act — Model Internal Committee Training Curriculum
summary: The Ministry has circulated a model training curriculum for Internal Committee members to state governments, covering inquiry procedure, evidence handling and confidentiality obligations, for voluntary adoption by employers and District Officers in structuring Committee member training.

case: Factory-Specific POSH Compliance Circular for Multi-Shift Establishments
headline: POSH Act — Compliance Circular for Factories and Industrial Establishments
summary: A state labour department has issued a circular directing factories and industrial establishments operating multiple shifts to ensure Internal Committee accessibility and complaint-reporting channels are available across all shifts, and to extend Committee jurisdiction expressly to contract and apprentice workers on the factory floor.

case: Payment of Gratuity Act — Ceiling Revision Under Consideration
headline: Gratuity Ceiling — Proposed Revision
summary: The government is reported to be reviewing a further upward revision of the statutory gratuity ceiling under the Payment of Gratuity Act, continuing the pattern of periodic upward revisions in recent years.

case: State Amendment to Contract Labour (Regulation & Abolition) Act Rules
headline: Contract Labour Act — State Rule Amendment
summary: A state government has notified amendments to its Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act rules, revising the employee-threshold and licensing renewal process applicable to contractors and principal employers within the state.

case: Maternity Benefit Act — Renewed Emphasis on Crèche Facility Compliance
headline: Maternity Benefit Act — Crèche Obligation
summary: The Ministry has renewed its compliance emphasis on the crèche facility obligation for establishments employing the statutory threshold number of employees, reiterating that the obligation applies regardless of the gender composition of the workforce actually availing it.

case: Model Standing Orders Updated for Fixed-Term Employees
headline: Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) — Fixed-Term Employment
summary: The Central Government's Model Standing Orders continue to be applied to clarify parity obligations for fixed-term employees relative to permanent employees performing similar work, following their introduction alongside the Industrial Relations Code framework.

case: Payment of Bonus Act — Eligibility Wage Ceiling Notification Watch
headline: Payment of Bonus Act — Eligibility Ceiling
summary: Industry bodies have sought a revision of the eligibility wage ceiling under the Payment of Bonus Act, last revised some years ago, citing wage inflation since the previous notification; no formal revision has yet been notified.

case: Minimum Wages — Variable Dearness Allowance Revised
headline: Minimum Wages Act — VDA Revision
summary: A state labour department has notified its periodic revision of the variable dearness allowance component of minimum wages across scheduled employments, effective from the notified date.

case: Industrial Relations Code — Re-Skilling Fund Contribution Guidance
headline: Industrial Relations Code — Re-Skilling Fund
summary: The Ministry issued further guidance on employer contributions to the re-skilling fund for retrenched workers under the Industrial Relations Code, clarifying the contribution computation and disbursement timeline to affected workers.

case: Code on Wages, Industrial Relations Code, Social Security Code & OSH Code — Full Enforcement
headline: India's Four New Labour Codes Come Into Full Force, Repealing 29 Central Labour Statutes
summary: Following notification on 21 November 2025, the Code on Wages 2019, Code on Social Security 2020, Industrial Relations Code 2020 and Occupational Safety, Health & Working Conditions Code 2020 rolled out to full enforcement from 1 April 2026, consolidating 29 central labour statutes. The Social Security Code extends formal EPF/ESI-equivalent coverage to gig and platform workers for the first time, while the Wages Code

case: Full and Final Settlement — Preclusion of Termination Challenge
headline: Acceptance of Full and Final Settlement Bars Subsequent Challenge to Termination Legality
summary: The Bombay High Court held that an employee who accepts full and final settlement of dues upon termination cannot subsequently challenge the validity or legality of termination in a labour forum. The settlement operates as a binding compromise of all claims arising from the employment relationship, including unlawful termination claims.

case: EPF International Workers Provisions — Constitutional Validity
headline: Delhi HC Upholds Constitutional Validity of EPF Provisions for International Workers
summary: The Delhi High Court Division Bench upheld the constitutional validity of paragraphs 83 and 69 of the EPF Scheme relating to mandatory PF contributions for international workers (IW), reversing a Karnataka Single Judge decision that had struck down the IW provisions. The Bombay High Court's earlier ruling upholding validity was followed.

case: Four Labour Codes — Implementation Notification
headline: Central Government Notifies Unified Implementation of All Four Labour Codes Effective November 21, 2025
summary: The Ministry of Labour and Employment notified the implementation of all Four Labour Codes — Code on Wages 2019, Code on Social Security 2020, Industrial Relations Code 2020, and Code on Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions 2020 — with effect from November 21, 2025. This is a historic consolidation of 29 central labour laws into four codes.

case: Karnataka Mandatory Menstrual Leave Policy
headline: Karnataka Introduces Mandatory Paid Menstrual Leave for Women Employees
summary: The Karnataka government introduced a policy mandating paid menstrual leave for women employees in the state, joining a small number of states offering such statutory protection. Employers operating in Karnataka must implement and communicate this leave entitlement as part of their HR framework.

case: POSH Act — IC Jurisdiction Against Perpetrator From a Different Organisation
headline: Internal Committee of Aggrieved Woman's Workplace Has Jurisdiction Against Perpetrators From Different Organisations
summary: The Supreme Court clarified that an Internal Committee (IC) constituted at the aggrieved woman's workplace is empowered to inquire into a complaint even where the respondent is an employee of a different department or organisation. The IC's jurisdiction follows the complainant, not the perpetrator.

case: EDLI Amendment Scheme 2025
headline: Employees' Deposit-Linked Insurance Scheme Amended — Enhanced Death Benefit Coverage
summary: The Ministry of Labour and Employment notified the Employees' Deposit-Linked Insurance (Amendment) Scheme, 2025 (effective July 19, 2025), significantly enhancing insurance coverage available to EPF members and providing increased death benefit coverage to nominees.

case: Maternity Benefit Act — Contract Employees
headline: Contract Employees Entitled to Full Maternity Benefits Even If Benefits Exceed Contract Duration
summary: The Supreme Court held that once entitlement criteria under the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961 are fulfilled, an employee is entitled to full maternity benefits even if those benefits exceed the duration of her contract. Terminating or declining to renew the contract during the maternity period constitutes prohibited 'discharge' under Section 12(2)(a) of the Act.

case: Code on Wages 2019 — Implementation Watch
headline: Four Labour Codes — Central Government Finalises Implementation Readiness Ahead of November 2025
summary: The Central Government in early 2025 continued finalisng state-level rules under all Four Labour Codes — Code on Wages, Code on Social Security, Industrial Relations Code, and the Code on Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions — in preparation for unified implementation across states.

case: Food Safety and Standards (Licensing and Registration of Food Businesses) Amendment Regulations, 2026
headline: FSSAI Licences Become Perpetually Valid — Renewal Cycle Scrapped, Street Vendors Get Deemed Registration
summary: Notified on 10 March 2026 and effective 1 April 2026, the amendment grants perpetual validity to FSSAI licences and registrations issued thereafter, ending the one-to-five-year renewal cycle; introduces deemed registration for street food vendors; brings in a risk-based inspection and food-safety-audit framework; and revises turnover thresholds — basic registration up to ₹1.5 crore, State Licence between ₹1.5 crore a

case: Standing Committee on Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution — Report to Parliament
headline: House Panel Presses FSSAI to Notify Front-of-Pack Labelling Rules After Four-Year Delay
summary: A parliamentary standing committee report tabled in Parliament expressed being "dismayed" that the draft Front-of-Pack Nutrition Labelling (FOPNL) Regulations — first notified in September 2022 and attracting over 14,000 stakeholder comments — remain pending, and recommended clear, colour-coded "at-a-glance" warning labels for products high in sugar, salt, or fat, together with tighter monitoring of packaged foods so

case: Food Safety and Standards (Labelling and Display) First Amendment Regulations, 2026
headline: FSSAI Tightens Rules on "Natural" Claims, Nutrition Disclosures and Infant Nutrition Labelling
summary: Notified on 24 March 2026 and set to take force from 1 July 2027, the amendment revises the 2020 Labelling and Display Regulations across several fronts: infant nutrition products are exempted from disclosing per-serve %RDA contribution and servings-per-pack; packages up to 100 sq. cm no longer require the FSSAI logo (though multi-unit packs still must carry it); and limits are reinforced on misleading "100% natural"

case: In re: Front-of-Pack Labelling for HFSS Foods — SC Supervision
headline: FSSAI Tells SC It Is Still Weighing Pictorial vs. Tabular Warning Label Formats
summary: Responding to a 10 February 2026 Supreme Court order urging it to mandate front-of-pack labels on packaged foods high in fat, sugar, or salt, FSSAI filed an affidavit stating it was still evaluating tabular versus pictorial warning formats and sought a further six weeks to submit a detailed proposal. The Court had earlier expressed dissatisfaction that FSSAI's compliance efforts "had not yielded any positive or good

case: FSSAI — Contempt Warning; Continued Judicial Monitoring
headline: FOPL and Nutraceutical Regulations Under Active SC Monitoring — Contempt of Court Threshold Approaching
summary: The Supreme Court continues to monitor FSSAI's compliance with its directions on front-of-pack labelling and nutraceutical regulation. Repeated failures to meet court deadlines have brought the matter close to the contempt threshold. The Court has indicated that further delay will attract personal liability of senior FSSAI officials.

case: FSSAI Warning Labels — Packaged Foods
court: Supreme Court — Bench of Justices Pardiwala & Viswanathan
headline: SC Asks FSSAI to Evaluate 'Warning Label' Model for High Sugar, Salt and Fat Packaged Foods
summary: The Supreme Court's bench directed FSSAI to evaluate whether packaged food items with excessive sugar, salt, and saturated fat should carry prominent front-of-pack warning labels — potentially modelled on Chile's 'black octagons' system. FSSAI was given time to consult stakeholders and present an action plan, in a PIL citing the rising prevalence of diabetes, obesity, and heart disease.

case: FSSAI Mobile Food Testing Laboratory Expansion — GeM Bids
headline: FSSAI Expands Field Enforcement Capacity Through Mobile Food Testing Laboratories Nationwide
summary: FSSAI issued procurement bids in early 2026 for Mobile Food Testing Laboratories (MFTLs) at regional and branch offices, enabling on-the-spot field testing at markets, warehouses, and transport hubs. MFTLs allow near-immediate test results — significantly improving FSSAI's capacity to initiate enforcement action at any point in the food supply chain without waiting for fixed-lab results.

case: NABL-Accredited Laboratories List Updated — Import Testing Enhanced
headline: FSSAI Notifies Updated List of NABL-Accredited Laboratories; Food Import Rejection Notices Increased
summary: FSSAI updated and gazetted its list of NABL-accredited laboratories under Section 43(1) FSSA in January 2026. Import testing at ports of entry is now exclusively through certified labs. Food Import Rejection Orders have increased significantly, particularly for products with non-conforming pesticide or contaminant levels, published on the Food Import Rejection Alert (FIRA) portal.

case: Draft FOPL Regulations Deferred for Further Consultation
headline: FSSAI's 49th Central Advisory Committee Defers Final FOPL Regulations — Implementation Window Extended
summary: The FSSAI's 49th Central Advisory Committee meeting deferred final notification of FOPL regulations pending further stakeholder consultation and technical review. Major food industry players including ITC, Nestlé, Britannia, and HUL engaged actively in the consultation process. The Supreme Court has continued monitoring FSSAI's compliance.

case: ORS Brand Name Order — Issued and Subsequently Withdrawn
headline: FSSAI Issues and Then Revokes Prohibition on Using 'ORS' Alongside Brand Names
summary: FSSAI's October 14 order prohibiting the use of the term 'ORS' alongside brand names caused significant market disruption in the oral rehydration salt category. Following intensive industry representations, FSSAI subsequently withdrew the order. The episode underscores the importance of active surveillance of FSSAI gazette notifications by manufacturers.

case: FSSAI — Court Monitoring; One Final Extension Granted
headline: SC Grants Final Extension to October 2025 on FOPL Regulations — Contempt Warning Issued
summary: After FSSAI failed to meet the April 2025 FOPL deadline, the Supreme Court granted a final extension to October 2025 to notify front-of-pack labelling regulations, issuing a strong warning that further non-compliance would result in contempt proceedings against FSSAI officials.

case: FSSAI Commissioner — Section 30 Emergency Orders Must Be Evidence-Based
headline: Emergency Prohibition Orders Under Section 30 Set Aside for Lack of Evidence-Based Foundation
summary: Courts consistently held in 2025 that the Commissioner of Food Safety must rely on objective evidence and a Designated Officer's report confirming a health risk before issuing emergency prohibition orders under Section 30 FSSA. Orders issued on suspicion without the requisite report — even for high-profile cases — were set aside as procedurally defective.

case: FSSA Section 59 — Life Imprisonment for Adulteration Causing Death Confirmed
headline: Life Imprisonment Under Section 59 FSSA for Fatal Food Adulteration Is Enforceable
summary: Courts confirmed in 2025 that Section 59 FSSA provides a graduated penalty scheme up to life imprisonment (minimum 7 years) where adulterated or sub-standard food results in death. Following Ram Nath (2024), simultaneous IPC prosecution is barred — but this does not diminish FSSA penalties. The FSSA penalty framework is among India's most stringent regulatory deterrents.

case: FSSAI Advisory — Prohibition of '100%' Claims on Food Labels
headline: FSSAI Prohibits Use of '100%' Claims Such as '100% Natural' or '100% Juice' on Labels
summary: FSSAI issued a formal advisory prohibiting food businesses from using absolute '100%' claims (e.g., '100% Natural', '100% Juice', '100% Pure') on food labels, finding such claims mislead consumers by creating unrealistic expectations about product purity. Food businesses were directed to amend labels accordingly.

case: FSSAI Directive — Illegal Fruit Ripening and Synthetic Coatings
headline: FSSAI Directs States to Intensify Crackdown on Illegal Calcium Carbide Fruit Ripening
summary: FSSAI directed all states and UTs to intensify inspections against illegal fruit ripening using calcium carbide and prohibited synthetic coatings on produce. Permitted alternatives such as ethylene gas at permissible concentrations were listed. Courts upheld significant penalties — including prosecution of owners and managers — for use of prohibited ripening agents.

case: FSS (Labelling & Display) Draft Amendment Regulations, February 2025
headline: FSSAI Issues Draft Front-of-Pack Labelling Regulations — Bold Nutritional Disclosure Required
summary: FSSAI notified Draft Food Safety and Standards (Labelling and Display) Amendment Regulations in February 2025 requiring nutritional information in bold text on the front of pack for all packaged food products. The draft was placed before the 49th FSSAI Central Advisory Committee meeting for stakeholder consultation.

case: FSSAI Platform Liability — Multi-Court Confirmation
headline: Online Food Platforms Are Food Business Operators — Co-Liable for Unlicensed Seller Violations
summary: Multiple High Courts confirmed that online food delivery platforms (Zomato, Swiggy, etc.) qualify as Food Business Operators under Section 3(1)(o) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, bearing co-liability for food safety violations by sellers on their platform. Platforms onboarding sellers without verifying FSSAI licences are directly exposed to prosecution under the FSSA.

case: In re: Front-of-Pack Labelling for HFSS Foods — Supreme Court Supervision (September 2026 Hearing)
headline: Supreme Court Questions FSSAI's Phased, Multi-Nutrient-First Approach to Red Hexagon Warning Labels
summary: FSSAI's 28 August 2026 affidavit proposed a two-phase rollout of interpretive warning labels — Phase 1 for products high in two or more nutrients of concern, Phase 2 for products high in any single nutrient. The Court questioned this approach and how ultra-processed foods would be treated, directing further affidavits within 10 days; next listed 28 September 2026.

case: FSSAI Advisory — Choosing Between Basic Registration and a Licence
headline: FSSAI Issues Clarificatory Advisory on Distinguishing Basic Registration From State/Central Licensing
summary: FSSAI issued a clarificatory advisory addressing recurring confusion among small food businesses over whether Basic Registration or a full State/Central Licence applies to their operations, reiterating that the distinguishing factor is annual turnover: Basic Registration for turnover up to ₹1.5 crore, State Licence between ₹1.5 crore and ₹50 crore, and Central Licence above ₹50 crore or for specified categories such

case: Hygiene Rating Scheme — Expanded State Rollout
headline: FSSAI's Voluntary Hygiene Rating Scheme Sees Expanded Rollout Across More States and Municipal Bodies
summary: Several additional states and municipal corporations formally adopted or expanded FSSAI's voluntary Hygiene Rating Scheme in early 2026, under which trained auditors assess restaurants and food outlets against defined hygiene parameters and assign a displayed star rating. Participation remains voluntary at the central level, though some municipal bodies have begun actively encouraging or, for select high-footfall cat

case: Packaged Drinking Water — Dual FSSAI-BIS Compliance Reaffirmed
headline: FSSAI Reaffirms That Packaged Drinking Water Requires Both FSSAI Licensing and BIS Certification
summary: FSSAI issued a reminder circular reaffirming that packaged drinking water and packaged natural mineral water manufacturers must hold both an FSSAI licence and BIS certification under the relevant Indian Standard, and that BIS certification does not substitute for FSSAI licensing or vice versa; the two regimes operate independently and address different aspects of compliance for the same product category.

case: Organic Food Certification — Jaivik Bharat Logo Enforcement
headline: FSSAI Tightens Enforcement Against Unauthorised Use of the 'Jaivik Bharat' Organic Logo
summary: FSSAI announced intensified enforcement against food businesses displaying organic claims or the 'Jaivik Bharat' logo without valid certification under either the National Programme for Organic Production or the Participatory Guarantee System, following a rise in unverified organic labelling complaints. Businesses were reminded that organic claims require current certification under one of the two recognised framewor

case: Food Fortification — Staple Category Compliance Reminder
headline: FSSAI Reminds Manufacturers of Fortified Staples of Mandatory Compliance Thresholds Under +F Logo Guidelines
summary: FSSAI issued a reminder to manufacturers marketing fortified staples (edible oil, milk, wheat flour and rice among others) under the '+F' logo, that use of the logo is conditional on meeting the prescribed micronutrient fortification thresholds under the Food Safety and Standards (Fortification of Foods) Regulations, and that displaying the logo on a batch that has not been verified as meeting those thresholds is a l

case: Deemed Registration for Street Food Vendors — Implementation Guidance
headline: FSSAI Issues Implementation Guidance for Deemed Registration of Street Food Vendors Under the 2026 Amendment
summary: Following the 2026 amendment introducing deemed registration for street food vendors, FSSAI issued follow-up implementation guidance clarifying the simplified documentation vendors must retain, the categories of hawking and mobile food sale covered, and the basic hygiene standards vendors are still expected to observe despite the simplified registration route; deemed registration eases the entry threshold but does no

case: Risk-Based Audit Framework — Expanded Third-Party Agency Empanelment
headline: FSSAI Expands List of Empanelled Third-Party Food Safety Audit Agencies Under the Risk-Based Framework
summary: FSSAI expanded its list of empanelled third-party food safety audit agencies as part of the risk-based inspection and audit framework introduced by the 2026 licensing amendment, adding agencies with regional coverage in previously under-served states and clarifying product-category-specific accreditation scope for existing empanelled agencies.

case: Spice and Condiment Adulteration — Nationwide Surveillance Drive
headline: FSSAI Directs States to Intensify Surveillance Sampling of Spices and Condiments Following Adulteration Complaints
summary: FSSAI directed state food safety authorities to intensify surveillance sampling of spices and condiments (particularly turmeric, chilli powder and mixed masala blends) following a rise in complaints and sample failures relating to unpermitted colouring agents, foreign starch adulteration and lead chromate contamination, with priority given to wholesale spice markets and repackaging units.

case: Liquor Licensing — Clarifying the FSSAI/Excise Licensing Boundary
headline: FSSAI Clarifies That Excise Licensing for Alcoholic Beverages Does Not Substitute for FSSAI Registration Where Applicable
summary: FSSAI issued a clarificatory note addressing confusion among hospitality and liquor retail businesses over the boundary between state excise licensing for alcoholic beverages and FSSAI's own registration or licensing requirements, noting that certain categories of establishment serving both food and alcohol (such as bars, restaurants and hotels) require FSSAI compliance for the food component of their operations inde

case: Labelling and Display Regulations — Implementation FAQ Released
headline: FSSAI Releases Implementation FAQ Ahead of the July 2027 Labelling and Display Amendment Deadline
summary: Ahead of the 1 July 2027 implementation deadline for the Food Safety and Standards (Labelling and Display) First Amendment Regulations, 2026, FSSAI released a set of implementation FAQs addressing common industry queries on the infant-nutrition disclosure exemptions, the revised FSSAI-logo threshold for small packages, and how the tightened restrictions on 'natural' and similar marketing claims will be assessed on ex

case: Jaypee Homebuyer PIL — Notice Issued to Standard Chartered & Consortium Lenders
headline: SC Issues Notice Seeking ED Probe and RBI Audit of Banks' Exposure to Stalled Real Estate Projects
summary: A Bench led by the Chief Justice issued notice on a PIL brought by a homebuyer alleging diversion of Jaypee Group funds, seeking an Enforcement Directorate probe and an RBI audit of Standard Chartered Bank and consortium lenders' end-use monitoring of loans extended to the group. The plea puts a spotlight on whether lenders adequately monitored how project finance was actually deployed by a borrower now in insolvency

case: M.R. Vasumathi & E. Muthurathinasabathy — SARFAESI Rule 9 Judgments
headline: Rule 9 Payment Timelines Under the SARFAESI Enforcement Rules Are Mandatory, Not Directory
summary: The Supreme Court held that the payment timelines prescribed under Rule 9 of the Security Interest (Enforcement) Rules, 2002 — governing deposit of sale consideration following a SARFAESI auction — are mandatory. A secured creditor's failure to strictly enforce these timelines, or a purchaser's failure to comply with them, can vitiate the auction sale, directly affecting borrowers' redemption rights under Section 13(

case: PIL on Public Sector Bank-ARC Settlements — Notice Issued
headline: SC Flags Bank–ARC–Borrower Nexus Over Deep-Discount Loan Settlements
summary: A bench led by the Chief Justice issued notice to the Centre, the RBI, and other respondents on a plea alleging that ₹1,537 crore owed to public sector banks was settled through two asset reconstruction companies for only ₹73.50 crore. The Court flagged mis-utilisation of public money as its central concern while acknowledging limits on its role in second-guessing banks' commercial wisdom on stressed-loan resolution.

case: RBI (NBFC — Responsible Business Conduct) (Second Amendment) Directions, 2026
headline: RBI Introduces Comprehensive New Chapter Governing NBFC Marketing & Third-Party Product Sales
summary: The RBI notified a new chapter under its 2025 Directions governing how NBFCs (including housing finance companies) advertise, market, and sell both their own and third-party financial products and services — tightening disclosure, suitability, and conduct standards for cross-selling arrangements.

case: Fraud Account Classification — Forensic Audit Disclosure Requirement
headline: Banks Need Not Grant a Personal Hearing Before Classifying an Account as Fraud, But Must Share the Forensic Audit Report
summary: The Supreme Court held that banks are not obligated to grant customers a personal oral hearing before classifying their accounts as fraud, accepting submissions that individual hearings are impractical given the scale of fraud cases. However, before such classification, banks must furnish the customer with the forensic audit report underlying the decision.

case: RBI Digital Payments & Loan Recovery Conduct Package, 2026
headline: Mandatory Additional Factor of Authentication for All Digital Payments Takes Effect
summary: RBI's sweeping April 2026 regulatory package mandates Additional Factor of Authentication (AFA) across every digital payment channel, introduces a restructured digital fraud compensation framework with revised customer-liability limits, and tightens the code of conduct for loan recovery agents, including mandatory training certification and grievance-escalation protocols.

case: LCR Framework Revision — Digital Banking Run-Off Factors
headline: RBI's Revised Liquidity Coverage Ratio Framework Expected to Implement From April 2026
summary: RBI's draft circular (released July 2024) revising the Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR) framework — proposing additional run-off factors for digitally-enabled deposits that can be rapidly withdrawn via mobile banking — is expected to be finalised and implemented from April 2026. Banks with high digitally-enabled deposit bases will face increased liquidity buffer requirements.

case: Banking Group Compliance Plans — Submission Deadline March 31, 2026
headline: Banks Must Submit Group-Level Compliance Plans to RBI by March 31, 2026
summary: Under the RBI's December 5, 2025 group-level regulation circular, all banking groups must submit plans for compliance with investment restrictions, AIF/REIT/InvIT caps, and overlapping product elimination to the RBI by March 31, 2026. No new overlapping product business may be commenced between the bank and its group entities after April 1, 2026.

case: SARFAESI Pre-Deposit — Must Be Deposited With DRAT, Not With Bank
headline: Section 18 SARFAESI Pre-Deposit for Appeal Must Be Made Directly With DRAT
summary: The Kerala High Court clarified that the mandatory pre-deposit required under Section 18 SARFAESI for filing an appeal must be deposited directly with the Debts Recovery Appellate Tribunal (DRAT) — not with the lending bank. Deposits made directly with the bank do not satisfy the Section 18 pre-condition for appeal admission.

case: Sabka Bima Sabki Raksha (Insurance Amendment) Bill, 2025 — Passed
headline: Parliament Passes Major Insurance Reform Bill — Wide-Ranging Statutory Changes to Insurance Laws
summary: Parliament passed the Sabka Bima Sabki Raksha Bill in January 2026, introducing wide-ranging reforms to India's insurance framework including revised capital requirements for insurers, expanded bancassurance and composite insurance licences, revised product and distribution norms, and enhanced policyholder protection provisions.

case: RBI Ombudsman Second Review Direction — Stayed
headline: Delhi HC Stays Order Directing Second Level Human Review for RBI Ombudsman-Rejected Complaints
summary: The Delhi High Court stayed a single judge's order that had directed a mandatory second level of human review for complaints rejected by the RBI Integrated Ombudsman. The stay leaves banks' existing complaint resolution processes intact pending further adjudication on whether the Ombudsman process meets natural justice requirements.

case: SME Pump-and-Dump — 26 Individuals Barred from Securities Markets
headline: SEBI Bars 26 Individuals for Coordinated Price Manipulation in SME-Listed Company
summary: SEBI barred 26 individuals from securities markets for coordinated price manipulation in DU Digital Technologies, an SME-listed company. Structured buying inflated prices, followed by coordinated selling at the peak. The case reinforces SEBI's intensifying surveillance of the SME IPO and listing segment.

case: RBI Group-Level Regulation Circular — December 5, 2025
headline: RBI Imposes Major Group-Level Regulatory Restrictions on Banks and Their Group Entities
summary: The RBI issued a significant circular imposing group-level regulatory restrictions on banks and their subsidiaries, associates, and JVs. Key changes include: the 'exclusivity principle' prohibiting product duplication between a bank and its group entities (effective April 1, 2026); investment restrictions on Category III AIFs; and new group-wide capital and risk management requirements. Compliance plans must be submi

case: OTS Scheme — Borrower Entitlement
headline: Writ Dismissed — Borrowers Cannot Claim One Time Settlement as a Matter of Legal Right
summary: The Kerala High Court dismissed a writ appeal where borrowers claimed entitlement to the benefit of a bank's One Time Settlement scheme. The Court held that OTS schemes are discretionary instruments — banks retain the right to reject applications that do not meet eligibility criteria. There is no vested legal right to an OTS, and judicial review of OTS rejection is limited.

case: RBI Master Direction on Wilful Defaulters — Two-Stage Committee Process Reiterated
headline: RBI Reiterates the Mandatory Two-Stage Identification and Review Committee Process Before Wilful Defaulter Classification
summary: Following a spate of classification challenges before High Courts, RBI has reiterated through supervisory communication to banks that the Master Direction on Treatment of Wilful Defaulters requires strict, sequential completion of both the Identification Committee's show-cause stage and the Review Committee's independent, reasoned confirmation before any classification is finalised; a compressed or parallel process d

case: Prudential Framework for Resolution of Stressed Assets — Continued Applicability
headline: RBI Clarifies Stressed-Asset Resolution Framework Continues to Govern Restructuring Outside Formal Insolvency
summary: RBI has clarified, in response to sector queries, that its Prudential Framework for Resolution of Stressed Assets (covering Special Mention Account classification, Inter-Creditor Agreements and the resolution review period) continues to apply to lender-led restructuring of stressed loans outside formal IBC proceedings, and lenders cannot bypass its early-identification and review-period requirements by characterising

case: Periodic Re-KYC Intervals and Video-KYC Norms — Updated
headline: RBI Updates Periodic Re-KYC Intervals and Expands Permitted Use of Video-Based Customer Identification
summary: RBI has updated its Master Direction on KYC to refine the periodic re-KYC intervals applicable to different customer risk categories and to expand the range of onboarding and re-verification scenarios in which banks may rely on Video-based Customer Identification Process (V-CIP) in place of in-person verification, subject to prescribed technical and audit-trail safeguards.

case: Fair Lending Practice — Penal Charges Circular — One-Year Compliance Review
headline: RBI's Penal Charges Framework — Supervisory Review Finds Continuing Instances of Disguised Penal Interest
summary: A year after RBI's circular barring compounded 'penal interest' in favour of clearly disclosed, non-compounded 'penal charges', RBI's supervisory review has flagged continuing instances of lenders effectively re-labelling penal interest as a recurring 'fee' that is, in substance, still compounded, prompting a fresh advisory to regulated entities to review loan documentation and system-level interest computation logic

case: Co-Lending Model Guidelines — Grievance Redressal Amendment
headline: RBI Amends Co-Lending Model Guidelines to Require a Single-Point Grievance Redressal Mechanism
summary: RBI has amended its co-lending model guidelines to require the partner bank and NBFC in a co-lending arrangement to jointly establish a single-point grievance redressal mechanism for borrowers, so that a customer does not have to separately pursue both lenders to resolve a single account-level grievance arising from the jointly-funded loan.

case: Payment Aggregator Authorisation Norms — Net-Worth and Escrow Compliance
headline: RBI Tightens Net-Worth and Escrow Account Compliance Timelines for Payment Aggregators
summary: RBI has tightened compliance timelines for payment aggregators under its authorisation framework, including revised net-worth thresholds for continued authorisation and stricter escrow account reconciliation and reporting requirements intended to ensure merchant settlement funds are not commingled with the aggregator's own operating funds.

case: Forex Compliance for Banks — Authorised Dealer Reporting Tightened
headline: RBI Tightens FEMA Reporting Obligations for Authorised Dealer Banks Handling Cross-Border Trade Transactions
summary: RBI has tightened reporting timelines and documentation standards applicable to Authorised Dealer banks handling cross-border trade and remittance transactions under FEMA, including closer scrutiny of underlying trade documentation for large-value import and export transactions to guard against trade-based structuring concerns.

case: Master Directions on Asset Reconstruction Companies — Valuation Disclosure
headline: RBI Strengthens Valuation Disclosure Requirements for Bank-to-ARC Stressed Loan Transfers
summary: RBI has strengthened disclosure requirements applicable to banks transferring stressed loans to asset reconstruction companies, requiring more detailed board-level documentation of the valuation methodology and the competitiveness of the sale process before a transfer is approved, particularly for public sector bank transactions attracting scrutiny over recovery discounts.

case: Deposit Insurance — Insured Claim Disbursal Timeline for Liquidated Banks
headline: DICGC Circular Reiterates Statutory Timeline for Disbursing Insured Deposit Claims After Bank Liquidation
summary: Following judicial directions in individual liquidation matters, the Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation has issued a circular reiterating that insured deposit claims of depositors of a bank placed under liquidation must be processed and disbursed within the statutorily prescribed period of receiving the liquidator's claim list, and cannot be deferred pending the liquidator's final settlement of the ba

case: Limitation for Latent-Defect Consumer Complaints
headline: Limitation for a Consumer Complaint Over a Latent Defect Runs From Discovery, Not the Date of Purchase
summary: Where a defect in goods or a deficiency in service is genuinely latent and not reasonably discoverable at the time of purchase, the two-year limitation period under Section 69 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 runs from the date of discovery, not the original transaction date. The discovery rule does not apply where the defect was reasonably apparent earlier.

case: ITC Ltd. — ITC Maurya Hotel Haircut Compensation Matter
headline: Supreme Court Sets Aside ₹2 Crore NCDRC Compensation Order for Want of Proof of Loss
summary: The Supreme Court set aside an NCDRC order directing ITC Maurya Hotel to pay ₹2 crore compensation to a model over a salon haircut, holding that the Commission had failed to assess how the complainant actually suffered a loss of that magnitude before fixing the award. The ruling reinforces that consumer compensation must be tethered to demonstrated loss, not awarded as a round-figure penalty.

case: Consumer Forum — Significant Damages in Telecom and Banking Deficiency
headline: Consumer Fora Award Significant Exemplary Damages for Telecom and Banking Service Deficiency
summary: Consumer fora across India consistently awarded significant exemplary damages in 2025-26 for deficiency of service by telecom operators and banks, including awards for mental agony and litigation costs well above the principal claim. Courts held that large corporate service providers must not treat consumer litigation as a negligible cost.

case: RERA Appellate Jurisdiction — Co-Location With Administrative Office
headline: SC Directs RERA Appellate Powers May Shift Alongside Office Relocation for Access to Justice
summary: While permitting Himachal Pradesh to shift its RERA office to Dharamshala, the Supreme Court directed that appellate powers may simultaneously shift to ensure litigants are not required to travel long distances to challenge RERA orders. The ruling reflects judicial awareness of access-to-justice concerns in regulatory appeals.

case: Unified RERA Portal — National Launch
headline: MoHUA Launches Unified National RERA Portal — All State Data Consolidated on One Platform
summary: The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs launched a unified RERA portal in September 2025, consolidating data from all state and UT RERA authorities on a single national platform. The portal enables homebuyers to check project registrations, complaint status, and developer compliance records across states from a single interface.

case: NCDRC — Informed Consent Standards in Medical Cases
headline: NCDRC Tightens Scrutiny of Hospital Consent Forms — Blanket Generic Consent Is Insufficient
summary: The NCDRC in multiple 2025 decisions heightened scrutiny of hospital consent forms, holding that blanket generic consent forms failing to disclose the specific risks of the actual procedure to be performed constitute evidence of negligence. Hospitals must demonstrate procedure-specific informed consent — identifying the exact risks of the operation performed.

case: Consumer Protection — Mental Agony and Litigation Costs
headline: Consumer Compensation Must Genuinely Account for Mental Agony and Litigation Costs
summary: In multiple 2025 consumer matters, the Supreme Court reinforced that compensation under the Consumer Protection Act must genuinely account for mental agony, harassment, and litigation costs — not merely the actual financial loss. Consumer fora were directed to award realistic, deterrent compensation that discourages repeat defaults by large service providers.

case: Consumer and Competition Act — Dual Remedies Available
headline: Consumer Forum and CCI Offer Concurrent Remedies for Unfair Trade Practices
summary: Courts confirmed that the Consumer Protection Act 2019 and the Competition Act 2002 offer overlapping but distinct remedies for unfair trade practices. Consumers affected by anti-competitive conduct by dominant players may simultaneously pursue consumer forum compensation claims and file information before the CCI.

case: Medical Negligence — Post-COVID Documentation Standards
headline: Courts Apply Heightened Documentary Scrutiny in Post-COVID Medical Negligence Cases
summary: Courts in 2025 applied heightened scrutiny to hospital documentation in post-COVID medical negligence cases — particularly ICU protocols, ventilator management, and medication records. Gaps in documentation were increasingly treated as an adverse inference of negligence rather than mere administrative oversight.

case: BNSS Transition — PMLA Post-July 2024 Complaints
headline: PMLA Complaints Filed After July 1, 2024 Must Comply With BNSS Section 223 Pre-Cognisance Hearing
summary: Courts confirmed that PMLA complaint proceedings filed after July 1, 2024 must comply with the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) pre-cognisance hearing requirement under Section 223. A cognisance order passed without affording the accused such a hearing was set aside as invalid.

case: PMLA — Continuing Offence Doctrine Applied
headline: Money Laundering Is a Continuing Offence Persisting as Long as Proceeds of Crime Are Held
summary: The Supreme Court held that the offence of money laundering under Section 3 PMLA is a continuing offence that persists as long as proceeds of crime remain in possession, use, or are projected as untainted funds. The timing of the predicate offence is irrelevant where possession and concealment continue. Aggregate transaction values — not individual transactions — must be considered for threshold purposes.

case: IBC Homebuyer Matters — Consolidated Directions
headline: RERA Is the Primary Forum for Homebuyers; IBC Must Not Be Used as a Debt Recovery Tool
summary: The Supreme Court confirmed across multiple homebuyer CIRP matters that RERA is the primary and appropriate forum for homebuyer grievances. The IBC should be invoked only for genuine project revival — not as debt recovery. The Court directed filling of NCLT/NCLAT vacancies on priority, creation of dedicated IBC benches for real estate, and formation of a high-level committee for systemic real estate sector reforms.

case: In Re: Pay and Allowances of the Members of the Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions (Suo Motu)
headline: Supreme Court Flags 'Quality Crisis' and Mounting Arrears Across Consumer Fora
summary: A Bench led by CJI Surya Kant, with Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohan, remarked that consumer commissions cannot function as rehabilitation posts for retired judges and bureaucrats, and directed the NCDRC President to file a status report on pendency, filings and disposal rates, floating the need for regional/circuit benches.

case: In Re: Functioning of State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions in Low-Pendency States (Suo Motu)
headline: Supreme Court Invokes Article 142 to Let High Court Judges Hear Consumer Appeals in States Without a Functioning Commission
summary: A Bench led by the Chief Justice, with Justice Joymalya Bagchi, invoked Article 142 of the Constitution to direct that sitting High Court judges in States and Union Territories that have found it not viable to constitute full-fledged State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions - including Sikkim, Manipur, Goa, Mizoram, Nagaland, Himachal Pradesh, the Andaman & Nicobar Islands and Meghalaya - will hear pending consu

case: Central Consumer Protection Authority — Product Recall Guidelines Enforcement
headline: CCPA Presses Manufacturers to Issue Timely Recall Notices Once a Safety Defect Is Confirmed
summary: The Central Consumer Protection Authority has emphasised that a manufacturer aware of a confirmed safety defect in goods already in the market is expected to issue a prompt, clearly publicised recall notice, rather than addressing the defect only through individual complaints as they arise.

case: Consumer Complaint Over 'Lifetime Warranty' Marketing Claim
headline: A 'Warranty' and a 'Guarantee' Are Not Interchangeable Terms, and a Seller's Marketing Must Reflect the Actual Terms Offered: State Commission
summary: A State Commission held that marketing a product with a 'lifetime warranty' claim, while the actual terms and conditions provided only a limited-period guarantee against manufacturing defects, misled the consumer as to the actual protection offered, and directed the seller to honour the marketed term.

case: Pecuniary Jurisdiction — District, State and National Commissions
headline: Pecuniary Jurisdiction of Consumer Commissions Is Based on the Value of Goods or Services Paid, Not the Compensation Claimed
summary: Consumer commissions have continued to apply the 2019 Act's jurisdictional structure strictly: the value of the goods or services paid for as consideration, not the amount of compensation ultimately claimed, determines whether a complaint properly belongs before the District Commission, the State Commission, or the National Commission.

case: Appellate Practice Note — Consumer Protection Act Appeals
headline: An Appeal From a District Commission Must Be Filed Within 45 Days, With Limited Scope for Condonation Absent Sufficient Cause
summary: Reiterating the appellate timeline under the Consumer Protection Act, the National Commission has emphasised that an appeal from a District Commission's order to the State Commission, or from a State Commission's order to the National Commission, must ordinarily be filed within 45 days, and that condonation of delay requires a genuinely sufficient cause rather than routine administrative explanations.

case: Execution Proceedings for Unpaid Consumer Commission Award
headline: A Consumer Commission Order Unpaid Within the Stipulated Period Attracts Enforcement as a Decree, Including Attachment of Property
summary: Where a party fails to comply with a consumer commission's order within the period specified, the order can be enforced in the same manner as a decree of a civil court, including through attachment and sale of property, and the commission itself retains jurisdiction to entertain execution proceedings without the successful party needing to file a fresh civil suit.

case: Passenger Consumer Complaint — Confirmed Berth Denial
headline: Denial of a Confirmed Railway Berth Without Adequate Cause Can Be Pursued as Deficiency in Service Before a Consumer Forum
summary: A consumer commission has confirmed that a passenger holding a confirmed railway reservation who is denied the allotted berth without adequate cause has a viable deficiency-in-service claim against the railway administration, independent of any separate remedy that may be available before the Railway Claims Tribunal for other categories of grievance.

case: Loan Foreclosure Charges Consumer Complaint
headline: Levying an Undisclosed Foreclosure Charge Not Specified in the Loan Agreement Is Deficiency in Service: State Commission
summary: A State Commission directed a lender to refund a foreclosure charge deducted from a borrower's prepayment amount, holding that a charge not clearly disclosed in the original loan agreement or sanction letter cannot be levied at the time of foreclosure merely because it appears in the lender's general, unreferenced fee schedule.

case: Consumer Mediation Cells — Uptake Since the 2019 Act
headline: Consumer Mediation Cells Attached to Commissions Are Seeing Increased Use for Disputes Centred on Remedy, Not Disputed Facts
summary: Consumer mediation cells established under the 2019 Act's mediation framework have seen steadily increasing referrals, particularly in disputes where the core disagreement concerns the appropriate remedy (such as the specifics of a replacement or refund) rather than genuinely contested facts requiring evidence.

case: Partition Suits — Non-Resident Co-Sharers
headline: A Partition Suit Cannot Be Rejected Merely Because Some Co-Sharers Reside Abroad
summary: The Supreme Court reaffirmed that residence outside India is not, by itself, a ground to reject or dismiss a partition suit at the threshold, so long as non-resident co-sharers can be validly served (through service outside India under the CPC, a power of attorney holder, or other recognised modes) and are properly represented in the proceedings.

case: Suits for Eviction of Trespassers by a Single Co-Owner
headline: A Single Co-Owner Can Sue to Evict a Trespasser Without Joining the Other Co-Owners
summary: Courts continue to apply the settled principle that any one co-owner of jointly held property, acting on behalf of the whole body of co-owners, can maintain a suit to evict a rank trespasser and recover possession, without needing to join every other co-owner as a party, since such a suit is treated as being for the benefit of all co-owners collectively.

case: Ex-Parte Interim Injunctions in Property Suits
headline: Courts Continue to Treat Ex-Parte Interim Injunctions in Property Disputes as the Exception, Not the Rule
summary: Reiterating settled practice, courts continue to hold that an ex-parte interim injunction disturbing a party's existing possession of property should be granted only in genuinely urgent circumstances, with specific reasons recorded for proceeding without first hearing the opposite party, and is expected to be revisited promptly once both sides are heard.

case: Wills Bequeathing Immovable Property — Suspicious Circumstances
headline: A Propounder of a Will Bequeathing Property Must Dispel Suspicious Circumstances, Not Just Prove Execution
summary: Courts continue to apply the settled principle that where a will disposing of immovable property is surrounded by suspicious circumstances (such as an unnatural exclusion of natural heirs, or the propounder's own active participation in preparing the will), the propounder bears the burden of clearly dispelling those circumstances, over and above the ordinary requirements of proving due execution and attestation.

case: Oral Family Partitions and Subsequent Memoranda
headline: A Memorandum Merely Recording an Earlier Oral Partition Does Not Require Registration
summary: Courts continue to draw a distinction between a document that itself effects a partition of immovable property (which requires registration) and a document that merely records, after the fact, a partition that had already taken place orally between the parties; the latter, being a memorandum rather than the operative instrument of partition, does not require registration to be relied upon.

case: Readiness and Willingness in Specific Performance Suits
headline: Readiness and Willingness Must Be Proved as a Continuing State of Affairs, Not Just at the Time of Filing
summary: Courts continue to hold that a plaintiff seeking specific performance of an agreement to sell property must demonstrate readiness and willingness to perform as a continuing state of affairs from the date of the agreement through the hearing of the suit, and not merely as a snapshot at the time the plaint was filed.

case: Mandatory Injunctions for Encroaching Construction
headline: A Mandatory Injunction to Remove Encroaching Construction Remains Available Where Encroachment Is Clearly Established
summary: Courts continue to grant mandatory injunctions directing removal of construction that has been clearly shown, typically with the support of a court commissioner's survey, to encroach beyond a party's boundary onto a neighbouring property, rather than limiting relief to a prohibitory injunction against further construction alone.

case: Lis Pendens — Notice Independent of Registration
headline: The Doctrine of Lis Pendens Applies Based on Pendency of the Suit, Independent of Any Separate Notice Registration
summary: Courts continue to clarify that the doctrine of lis pendens under Section 52 of the Transfer of Property Act operates from the mere pendency of a suit directly and specifically affecting title to the property, and does not depend on a separate notice of pending suit having been registered, in states that provide for such registration as an additional, non-mandatory safeguard.

case: Mutation Proceedings Yielding to Pending Civil Title Suits
headline: Revenue Mutation Proceedings Should Ordinarily Be Kept Pending Where a Civil Suit on Title Is Already Underway
summary: Continuing a settled line of guidance to revenue authorities, courts have reiterated that where a civil suit concerning title to a property is already pending, mutation proceedings before the revenue authority in respect of the same property should ordinarily await the outcome of that suit, given that mutation itself cannot conclusively determine a contested question of title.

case: Possession Suits Against Licensees After Revocation
headline: No Notice to Quit Is Required Before Suing a Licensee for Possession Once a Licence Is Revoked
summary: Courts continue to hold that a licensee's right to occupy property ends immediately upon valid revocation of the licence, and that, unlike a tenancy, no separate notice to quit is required before the licensor can institute a suit for possession against a licensee who continues to remain on the property after revocation.

case: RERA Institutional Effectiveness — Himachal Pradesh Relocation Matter
headline: Supreme Court Bench Says It May Be "Better to Abolish RERA" Than Let It Keep Favouring Defaulting Builders
summary: Hearing an appeal concerning relocation of the Himachal Pradesh RERA office, a bench led by the Chief Justice remarked that state RERAs appear to be "doing nothing but providing convenience to defaulting builders," and questioned whether the institution should be reconsidered altogether. The Court clarified that any actual abolition would require Parliament to amend or repeal the RERA Act — the remarks operate as ins

case: RERA Section 68 — Decriminalisation Amendment
headline: RERA Decriminalisation Amendment Narrows — But Does Not Eliminate — Penal Exposure for Developers
summary: The Jan Vishwas amendment to Section 68 of the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016 converts a defined set of criminal penalties into monetary ones, easing compliance friction for developers on procedural defaults. The reform is targeted rather than sweeping — RERA retains its penal character for substantive violations such as diversion of homebuyer funds and non-registration of projects.

case: GIDC Leasehold Rights — GST Exemption Confirmed
headline: Supreme Court Confirms Assignment of Industrial Leasehold Rights Is Not Subject to GST
summary: The Supreme Court dismissed the Revenue's Special Leave Petitions against a Gujarat High Court ruling that assignment, sale and transfer of leasehold rights in industrial plots allotted by state industrial development bodies are not a supply of service exigible to GST — settling a recurring point of dispute for industrial and warehousing transactions.

case: RERA Execution Mechanism — Bengaluru
headline: RERA Orders Are Not Civil Court Decrees — Execution Must Go Through the Statutory Recovery Mechanism
summary: The Karnataka High Court held that an order passed by a Real Estate Regulatory Authority does not amount to a civil court decree and cannot be executed through ordinary civil execution proceedings under the CPC. Enforcement of a RERA order must instead proceed through the statutory recovery mechanism specifically provided under the RERA Act itself — typically recovery as arrears of land revenue through the state's re

case: Land Acquisition Notifications — LARR Act, 2013
headline: Acquisition Notifications Issued Under the Repealed 1894 Land Acquisition Act Are Void Ab Initio, Even If Predating LARR's Commencement
summary: The Allahabad High Court held that acquisition notifications tied to the repealed Land Acquisition Act, 1894 are void ab initio where the acquiring authority failed to comply with the transitional and compensation requirements under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (LARR) — even where the original notification bore a date prior to the 1894

case: Model Disclosure Format for Structural Defect Liability Notices Under Section 14(3)
headline: RERA Authorities Standardise the Notice Format Homebuyers Must Use to Invoke the Five-Year Structural Defect Liability
summary: Several state RERA authorities have adopted a standardised written-notice format that an allottee must use to formally notify a promoter of a structural defect discovered within five years of possession, specifying the defect, the date of discovery, and a reasonable time for the promoter to rectify it before liability under Section 14(3) can be enforced through a complaint.

case: Force Majeure Extension Requests Under Section 6 — Documentary Standard Tightened
headline: RERA Authorities Tighten the Documentary Standard for Force Majeure-Based Project Registration Extensions
summary: Multiple state RERA authorities have tightened the evidentiary standard promoters must meet to obtain a registration extension under Section 6 on force majeure grounds, now requiring contemporaneous documentary proof (such as contractor correspondence, regulatory stop-work orders, or supply chain disruption notices) rather than a general narrative assertion that construction was delayed by circumstances beyond the pr

case: Homebuyer Association's Right to Inspect Common Area Handover Documents
headline: A Registered Apartment Owners' Association Is Entitled to Inspect the Promoter's Common Area Handover Records, High Court Holds
summary: A High Court has held that a registered apartment owners' association is entitled, as a matter of right flowing from RERA's conveyance and common-area provisions, to inspect the promoter's records relating to the specification, cost and handover status of common areas and facilities before executing any deed of conveyance or taking over maintenance responsibility.

case: Change in Sanctioned Layout Without Two-Thirds Allottee Consent — Penalty Upheld
headline: A Promoter Cannot Alter a Project's Sanctioned Layout Plan Without the Two-Thirds Allottee Consent Section 14 Requires
summary: A RERA Authority has upheld a penalty against a promoter who altered the sanctioned layout of a project (converting a portion of the originally disclosed open green area into an additional block of units) without first obtaining the written consent of at least two-thirds of the allottees, as mandated under Section 14(2) of RERA for any structural or layout alteration after registration.

case: Cancellation of Allotment by Allottee — Deduction Cap on Earnest Money
headline: A Promoter's Forfeiture on a Buyer-Initiated Cancellation Cannot Exceed the Earnest Money Cap Set by the Model Agreement
summary: A RERA Authority has reiterated that where an allottee voluntarily cancels a booking, the promoter's forfeiture on refund is capped at the earnest money percentage specified in the applicable state's model agreement for sale (typically a fixed percentage of the total consideration), and a promoter cannot additionally withhold processing fees, administrative charges or a further 'cancellation charge' layered on top of

case: Subvention Scheme Disclosure Requirements Tightened
headline: RERA Authorities Require Clearer Disclosure of Who Bears the Interest Cost Under a Subvention or Possession-Linked Payment Plan
summary: Following a rise in complaints, a RERA Authority has issued a circular requiring promoters offering subvention or possession-linked payment plans (where a bank disburses the loan to the developer progressively but the developer, not the buyer, services the interest until possession) to disclose in the agreement for sale exactly which party bears the interest cost if possession is delayed beyond the promised date, and

case: TDR Certificate Issued to a Developer Cannot Be Unilaterally Revoked Absent a Hearing
headline: A Municipal Authority Cannot Revoke a Transferable Development Rights Certificate Without Giving the Holder a Hearing
