summary: A High Court has held that a municipal or development authority cannot revoke or cancel a Transferable Development Rights (TDR) certificate already issued to a developer (including one that has since been sold to and is being utilised by a third party) without first issuing a show-cause notice and affording an opportunity of hearing, even where the revocation is premised on an alleged irregularity in the original lan

case: Revised Ready Reckoner Rates Affect Stamp Duty Computation for Under-Construction Units
headline: Revised Ready Reckoner Rates Change How Stamp Duty Is Computed for Units Booked Under Construction-Linked Plans
summary: A state government's annual revision of ready reckoner (circle) rates has changed the base valuation used to compute stamp duty on agreements for sale of under-construction units, with the relevant authority clarifying that the rate applicable is the one prevailing on the date of registration of the agreement for sale, not the rate prevailing on the date of initial booking or first payment.

case: Housing Society Maintenance Charges Cannot Be Levied Retrospectively Before Actual Handover
headline: A Promoter Cannot Charge Maintenance for a Period Before It Actually Handed Over Possession, Even If the Occupancy Certificate Predates Handover
summary: A RERA Authority has held that a promoter's demand for maintenance charges must be computed from the date possession was actually offered and handed over to the specific allottee, not from the earlier date on which the project's occupancy certificate was obtained, rejecting a promoter's attempt to backdate maintenance liability to the occupancy certificate date for units that were, in fact, handed over to individual

case: Affordable Housing Scheme Eligibility Verification Tightened Post-Allotment
headline: State Affordable Housing Scheme Introduces Post-Allotment Income Re-Verification to Curb Ineligible Beneficiary Retention
summary: A state housing department has introduced a post-allotment re-verification requirement for beneficiaries of its affordable housing scheme, requiring updated income and property-ownership declarations at defined intervals after possession, with allotments found to have relied on since-disproved eligibility declarations liable to cancellation and clawback of the subsidy component extended at booking.

case: Vikram Solar Limited — Section 9 Admission Set Aside
headline: NCLAT Sets Aside CIRP Admission Against Vikram Solar, Holding the Claim Fell Below the Rs. 1 Crore Section 4 Threshold
summary: The NCLAT set aside admission of the corporate insolvency resolution process against Vikram Solar Limited, holding that the underlying operational debt claim fell below the minimum threshold of Rs. 1 crore prescribed under Section 4 of the IBC for a Section 9 application, and that the application should not have been admitted in the first place.

case: KLSR Infratech Ltd. — Insolvency Quashed, Costs Imposed
headline: NCLAT Overturns NCLT Hyderabad Order Admitting Insolvency Against KLSR Infratech, Imposes Rs. 10 Lakh Costs
summary: The NCLAT, led by its Chairperson, overturned an NCLT Hyderabad order admitting insolvency proceedings against KLSR Infratech Ltd., setting aside the admission and imposing costs of Rs. 10 lakh, in a ruling reported to reflect the Tribunal's concern over attempts to misuse the insolvency process.

case: MCA Clarifies Board Process for Approving ESOP Scheme Amendments Mid-Vesting
headline: MCA Clarifies Board Process for Approving ESOP Scheme Amendments Mid-Vesting
summary: The Ministry of Corporate Affairs has clarified that a material amendment to an existing employee stock option scheme (such as altering the vesting schedule or exercise price for options already granted) requires fresh special resolution approval from shareholders and cannot be effected by the Nomination and Remuneration Committee acting alone, even where the original scheme document reserved some discretion to the C

case: Adjudicating Officers Increasingly Penalise Directors for Passive Non-Participation in Board Oversight
headline: Adjudicating Officers Increasingly Penalise Directors for Passive Non-Participation in Board Oversight
summary: Registrar of Companies adjudication orders through 2026 show a rising number of penalties against directors under Section 166 for failing to exercise independent judgment on transactions later found to be irregular, even where the director did not actively vote in favour and merely abstained without recorded objection.

case: SEBI Consults on Strengthening Drag-Along and Tag-Along Disclosure in Pre-IPO Shareholder Agreements
headline: SEBI Consults on Strengthening Drag-Along and Tag-Along Disclosure in Pre-IPO Shareholder Agreements
summary: SEBI has floated a consultation paper proposing that companies filing a draft red herring prospectus disclose the existence and key commercial terms of any drag-along or tag-along rights surviving in shareholder agreements post-listing, so prospective public investors can assess residual control and exit arrangements among pre-IPO shareholders.

case: Government Streamlines NCLT Filing Requirements for Schemes of Arrangement Under Sections 230-232
headline: Government Streamlines NCLT Filing Requirements for Schemes of Arrangement Under Sections 230-232
summary: The Ministry of Corporate Affairs has notified amendments simplifying the documentation required to be filed alongside an application for NCLT directions on convening scheme meetings, consolidating several previously separate affidavits into a single composite filing and standardising the format for valuation reports annexed to scheme petitions.

case: RBI Tightens Disclosure Around Corporate Guarantees Extended by NBFCs to Group Companies
headline: RBI Tightens Disclosure Around Corporate Guarantees Extended by NBFCs to Group Companies
summary: The Reserve Bank of India has updated its master direction on exposure norms to require NBFCs to separately disclose, in their financial statements, the aggregate value of corporate guarantees extended to group companies, along with the specific cross-default and cross-acceleration terms attached to each material guarantee.

case: Independent Directors' Databank Proficiency Self-Declaration Requirements Tightened
headline: Independent Directors' Databank Proficiency Self-Declaration Requirements Tightened
summary: The Ministry of Corporate Affairs has tightened the proficiency self-declaration requirements for individuals on the Independent Directors' Databank, requiring more detailed disclosure of prior directorships, disqualifications, and any regulatory proceedings, as part of the 'fit and proper' assessment infrastructure for independent directors.

case: Venture Capital Industry Body Issues Model Term Sheet Guidance on Exclusivity and Binding Clauses
headline: Venture Capital Industry Body Issues Model Term Sheet Guidance on Exclusivity and Binding Clauses
summary: A leading venture capital industry association has published non-binding model guidance recommending that term sheets clearly and separately label which clauses (typically exclusivity, confidentiality, governing law and cost allocation) are intended to bind the parties immediately, distinct from commercial terms expressed as subject to definitive documentation.

case: MCA21 Portal Adds Dedicated Workflow for Capital Reduction Petitions Under Section 66
headline: MCA21 Portal Adds Dedicated Workflow for Capital Reduction Petitions Under Section 66
summary: The Ministry of Corporate Affairs has introduced a dedicated e-filing workflow on the MCA21 portal for companies seeking NCLT confirmation of a reduction of share capital under Section 66, intended to standardise the documentation submitted to the Regional Director and Registrar ahead of the company's NCLT petition.

case: MCA's Renewed Strike-Off Drive Prompts a Wave of Section 252 Restoration Applications
headline: MCA's Renewed Strike-Off Drive Prompts a Wave of Section 252 Restoration Applications
summary: Following a fresh round of Registrar-initiated strike-offs of companies that failed to file annual returns for two consecutive years, company-law practitioners report a corresponding rise in Section 252 restoration applications before the NCLT, particularly from companies that were dormant but held unresolved assets, bank accounts, or pending litigation.

case: Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026
headline: Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill 2026 Set to Overhaul NCLT Scheme-of-Arrangement Procedure
summary: Now before the Joint Parliamentary Committee, the Bill proposes sweeping changes to Sections 230–233 of the Companies Act, 2013, streamlining NCLT scheme-of-arrangement procedures, revising creditor/shareholder meeting-class thresholds, clarifying cross-border merger rules for foreign companies, decriminalising a swathe of provisions, and removing the IBC cross-reference from Section 230(1). Multi-bench NCLT schemes

case: Competition (Amendment) Act, 2023 — Deal Value Threshold Guidance
headline: CCI Issues Fresh Clarificatory Guidance on Deal Value Threshold Filings
summary: Building on the Deal Value Threshold introduced by the Competition (Amendment) Act, 2023, the CCI in early 2026 published further clarifications addressing on-market share purchases, open offers, filing timelines and penalty methodology, prompting a fresh wave of compliance reviews across PE and strategic deal teams for asset-light, digital-economy targets that previously escaped scrutiny under the old asset/turnover

case: National Company Law Tribunal (Amendment) Rules, 2024 — 2026 Roll-Out
headline: NCLT Benches Directed to Dispose of Merger Petitions Within 90 Days
summary: NCLT benches nationwide have been directed to dispose of merger and amalgamation petitions within 90 days of filing, a significant compression compared to earlier practice where scheme approvals commonly took 8–12 months or longer, particularly where multiple benches had jurisdiction over different transacting entities.

case: CCI Digital Market Merger Surveillance — Ongoing Enforcement
headline: CCI Actively Reviewing Digital Market Acquisitions Under Deal Value Threshold
summary: The CCI in early 2026 is actively reviewing multiple digital sector acquisitions and investements under the new deal value threshold framework. Several pre-merger filings have been scrutinised for potential anti-competitive effects in data markets, platform economies, and digital financial services — signalling the CCI's intent to be an active regulator in the digital economy.

case: NCLT Trademark Jurisdiction Without Insolvency Link
headline: NCLT Cannot Exercise IBC Jurisdiction Over Pure IP Ownership Disputes Without Direct Insolvency Link
summary: The Supreme Court ruled that the NCLT lacks jurisdiction under Section 60(5)(c) IBC to adjudicate trademark or IP ownership disputes that have no direct connection with the ongoing insolvency proceedings. IP ownership is not 'arising out of or in relation to' insolvency merely because the IP is an asset of a corporate debtor.

case: SME IPO Tightened Norms — Following Market Manipulation Concerns
headline: SEBI Tightens SME IPO Norms After Widespread Manipulation Concerns in the Segment
summary: SEBI announced tightened norms for SME IPOs following widespread regulatory concerns about price manipulation, inflated valuations, and governance deficiencies in the SME listing segment. Key changes include enhanced due diligence requirements for merchant bankers, stricter promoter lock-in provisions, and more rigorous disclosure standards.

case: SEBI Board Meeting December 2025 — Major Regulatory Pipeline
headline: SEBI December 2025 Board Meeting Announces Significant 2026 Regulatory Changes
summary: SEBI's December 2025 Board meeting announced a pipeline of significant regulatory changes: revised Small and Medium REIT regulations, tightened SME IPO norms following manipulation concerns, revised Alternative Investment Fund regulations, and further LODR amendments affecting related-party transactions. Implementation timelines extend through mid-2026.

case: SEBI Insider Trading — Intensified Disgorgement Enforcement in 2025
headline: SEBI Issues Multiple Disgorgement Orders Against Insider Trading Using UPSI in 2025
summary: SEBI significantly intensified enforcement against insider trading in 2025, issuing multiple disgorgement orders requiring traders to surrender all profits from price-sensitive information. SEBI's expanded surveillance — including social media monitoring and advanced data analytics — identified trading patterns previously undetectable.

case: Companies (Accounts) Rules — POSH Disclosure Now Mandatory in Board's Report
headline: MCA Formalises Mandatory POSH Case Disclosure in Company Board's Report
summary: The MCA formalised requirements for companies to report on Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH) Act compliance in the Board's Report under the Companies Act, 2013. Companies must now disclose the number of POSH complaints filed, pending, and disposed of in the annual Board's Report — making POSH compliance a corporate governance accountability matter.

case: LPA Not Maintainable Against Single Judge IP Tribunal Orders
headline: LPA Is Not Maintainable Against Single Judge Orders in Trademark Appeals Under Section 91 TM Act
summary: The Calcutta High Court clarified the appellate framework under the Trade Marks Act, 1999: a Letters Patent Appeal is not maintainable against a Single Judge's order in an appeal under Section 91 of the Act. The IP Division's role in the trademark appeals hierarchy was clarified — direct challenges to IP tribunal rulings require fresh proceedings.

case: CCI Deal Value Threshold — Fully Operational
headline: CCI's New Deal Value Threshold for Merger Notifications Fully Operational From 2025
summary: The Competition (Amendment) Act, 2023's new deal value threshold became fully operational in 2025, requiring CCI pre-clearance for acquisitions of companies with substantial domestic market impact — even where they lack significant Indian assets. Digital economy M&A, data-rich startup acquisitions, and platform transactions now require CCI review.

case: SBO (Significant Beneficial Owner) Framework Revised
headline: SEBI Revises SBO Identification and Disclosure Framework for Listed Companies
summary: SEBI issued a revised circular tightening the Significant Beneficial Owner identification and disclosure framework, including stricter reporting timelines for indirect shareholding changes and an expanded definition of 'control' for SBO purposes — with significant implications for PE investors and promoter groups restructuring listed company holdings.

case: SEBI LODR Amendment — Material Event Disclosure Within 30 Minutes
headline: SEBI Tightens Material Event Disclosure — Listed Companies Must Disclose Within 30 Minutes of Occurrence
summary: SEBI's amended Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements (LODR) Regulations reduce the material event disclosure window to 30 minutes from occurrence for certain categories of events (previously 24 hours). The amendments also tightened related-party transaction frameworks, revised director appointment norms, and expanded the definition of events requiring immediate disclosure.

case: In re: Scheme of Amalgamation of Vidarbha Industries Power Limited with Adani Power Limited
court: National Company Law Tribunal, Mumbai Bench
headline: NCLT Mumbai Sanctions Adani Power's Merger of Vidarbha Industries Power, Completing a Ten-Subsidiary Consolidation
summary: The NCLT Mumbai Bench, comprising Judicial Member Vinay Goel and Technical Member Charanjeet Singh Gulati, sanctioned the scheme of amalgamation of Vidarbha Industries Power Limited (which operates a 600 MW thermal power plant in Nagpur) with its parent Adani Power Limited, with an appointed date of 1 April 2025. The order completes tribunal-level approval of Adani Power's consolidation of ten wholly owned subsidiari

case: Advance Ruling — ITC Eligibility on CSR Expenditure
headline: Authority for Advance Ruling Holds ITC Available on GST Paid for CSR-Mandated Expenditure
summary: An Authority for Advance Ruling has held that input tax credit is available on GST paid for goods and services procured to discharge a company's mandatory Corporate Social Responsibility obligations under Section 135 of the Companies Act, treating such expenditure as incurred in the course or furtherance of business rather than as a personal or non-business expense.

case: GSTAT Operationalisation — Transfer of Pending High Court Writ Matters
headline: High Courts Begin Transferring Pending GST Appeal-Stage Writ Petitions to the Now-Operational GST Appellate Tribunal
summary: With principal and state benches of the GST Appellate Tribunal now functional, several High Courts have begun disposing of writ petitions that were filed only because the Tribunal was not yet operational, directing petitioners to pursue their statutory appellate remedy before GSTAT instead, generally while protecting the limitation period already spent before the High Court.

case: Direct Tax Vivad se Vishwas Scheme — Compliance Deadline Watch
headline: CBDT Issues Clarifications on Eligible Disputes and Form Filing Timelines Under the Direct Tax Vivad se Vishwas Scheme
summary: The CBDT has issued clarificatory guidance on categories of pending appeals and disputes eligible for settlement under the Direct Tax Vivad se Vishwas scheme, and on the sequence and timelines for filing the prescribed declaration and undertaking forms, following queries from taxpayers on borderline eligibility cases involving partly adjudicated or remanded matters.

case: Benami Property — Confirmation of Provisional Attachment
headline: Appellate Tribunal Confirms Provisional Attachment of Property Under the Benami Transactions (Prohibition) Amendment Act
summary: The appellate authority under the Prohibition of Benami Property Transactions Act confirmed a provisional attachment order where the beneficial owner failed to satisfactorily explain the source of funds used to acquire a property held in the name of a third party, holding that a mismatch between the named holder's disclosed income and the property's value, combined with an unexplained fund trail, was sufficient to su

case: Black Money Act — Foreign Asset Disclosure Penalty Upheld
headline: High Court Upholds Penalty for Non-Disclosure of Foreign Bank Account Under the Black Money Act, Rejects Bona Fide Omission Plea
summary: A High Court upheld a penalty levied under the Black Money (Undisclosed Foreign Income and Assets) and Imposition of Tax Act, 2015, for failure to disclose a foreign bank account in the Schedule FA of the income tax return, rejecting the assessee's plea that the omission was a bona fide oversight given the account's low balance, and holding that the disclosure obligation under the Act is not contingent on the account

case: Tax Residency Certificate — DTAA Treaty Benefit Denial
headline: Treaty Benefit Under DTAA Cannot Be Denied Solely for a Formatting Defect in an Otherwise Valid Tax Residency Certificate: High Court
summary: A High Court set aside denial of Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement benefits where the assessing officer had rejected a Tax Residency Certificate issued by the foreign tax authority on the ground that it did not follow a specific prescribed format, holding that where the certificate otherwise establishes residency and the required particulars in substance, treaty benefit cannot be denied for a non-prescribed formatt

case: Place of Supply — Cross-Border Intermediary Services
headline: Advance Ruling Reiterates That Cross-Border Intermediary Services Are Taxed at the Supplier's Location, Not as an Export
summary: An Authority for Advance Ruling reaffirmed that where an Indian entity arranges or facilitates a supply of goods or services between a foreign principal and a third party without supplying the main service itself, its activity falls within the definition of 'intermediary' services under the IGST Act, placing the place of supply at the location of the intermediary in India rather than the recipient's location abroad,

case: Works Contract — Solar EPC Composite Supply Classification
headline: Solar Power EPC Contract Is a Composite 'Works Contract' Supply, Not a Separate Sale of Goods and Services: High Court
summary: A High Court upheld the department's classification of an engineering, procurement and construction contract for a solar power plant as a single composite works contract supply under Section 2(119) of the CGST Act, rejecting the taxpayer's attempt to artificially split the contract value into a separate goods supply (taxed at a concessional rate) and a services component, where the contract was in substance a single,

case: Prosecution for Alleged Wilful Tax Evasion — Sanction Defect
headline: High Court Quashes Prosecution for Alleged Wilful Evasion Where the Sanctioning Authority Did Not Independently Apply Its Mind
summary: A High Court quashed a criminal complaint alleging wilful attempt to evade tax, holding that the sanction for prosecution under Section 279 of the Income Tax Act must reflect the sanctioning authority's own independent application of mind to the material on record, and that a sanction order which merely reproduces the recommending officer's note without any distinct reasoning of its own does not satisfy this requirem

case: Stay of Demand — Revised Guidance on the 20% Pre-Deposit Benchmark
headline: CBDT Instruction Clarifies That the 20% Stay-of-Demand Benchmark Is Not a Rigid Floor Where a Strong Prima Facie Case Exists
summary: The CBDT has issued further guidance to field officers on the administratively set 20% pre-deposit benchmark for staying recovery of a disputed income tax demand pending first appeal, clarifying that officers retain discretion to grant a stay on a lower percentage, or on terms other than cash payment, where the assessee demonstrates a strong prima facie case supported by jurisdictional precedent or an identical issue

case: GST Treatment of Liquidated Damages & Penalty Clauses
headline: CBIC Clarifies When Liquidated Damages and Penalty Clauses Are — and Are Not — Exigible to GST
summary: CBIC guidance clarifies that liquidated damages, penalty clauses, and forfeiture of earnest money that are genuinely compensatory and intended to deter breach do not, without more, constitute consideration for a separate taxable "tolerating an act" supply under Schedule II of the CGST Act. Where the substance of a clause instead prices continued forbearance, GST exposure may still arise.

case: Validity of Section 16(2)(c), CGST Act, 2017
headline: Input Tax Credit Is Available to a Buyer Only If the Supplier Has Actually Paid Tax to the Government
summary: The Supreme Court affirmed a Gujarat High Court ruling upholding the constitutional validity of Section 16(2)(c) of the CGST Act, 2017, dismissing challenges that sought to decouple a buyer's Input Tax Credit entitlement from actual tax payment by the supplier. ITC remains conditional on the supplier discharging its tax liability, regardless of the buyer's own compliance.

case: Online Gaming — 28% GST on Full Face Value of Bets
headline: Supreme Court Upholds 28% GST on Full Value of Bets Placed on Online Gaming Platforms
summary: The Supreme Court upheld the levy of 28% GST on the full face value of bets placed through online gaming platforms, holding the levy valid even where the underlying game involves skill rather than chance, rejecting industry arguments that tax should apply only to platform commission or gross gaming revenue.

case: Indian Railways Cross-Subsidy Surcharge Appeals
headline: Indian Railways Remains Liable for Cross-Subsidy Surcharge on Open-Access Power Procurement
summary: A two-judge bench dismissed all appeals filed by Indian Railways, upholding APTEL's February 2024 order that Railways must pay Cross-Subsidy Surcharge and Additional Surcharge when procuring power through open access, rejecting Railways' claim to a blanket exemption from these regulatory charges.

case: In re: Procedure for Milestone Extension Charges for GNA Connectivity Grantees
headline: CERC Lets Renewable Developers Pay to Extend Missed Connectivity Milestones Instead of Losing Access Outright
summary: The CERC approved a procedure for levying graded Milestone Extension Charges that allows renewable energy generators, storage systems and renewable power park developers who are behind schedule on land-document submission, Financial Closure or Commercial Operation Date milestones under the CERC (Connectivity and General Network Access) Regulations, 2022 to pay for additional time, replacing the earlier regime of auto

case: In re: Revised Renewable Purchase Obligation Compliance and Penalty Framework
headline: SERC Notifies Revised Penalty Structure for Shortfall in Renewable Purchase Obligation Compliance
summary: A State Electricity Regulatory Commission has notified a revised, graded penalty structure for obligated entities (distribution licensees, open-access consumers and captive users) who fail to meet their annual Renewable Purchase Obligation (RPO) targets, replacing a flat non-compliance charge with a scale that increases with the size and persistence of the shortfall, while continuing to permit banking of RPO complian

case: Draft Amendment to Electricity (Rights of Consumers) Rules, 2020
headline: Draft Amendment Proposes Tighter Timelines for Distribution Licensees Under Universal Service Obligation
summary: The Ministry of Power has circulated a draft amendment to the Electricity (Rights of Consumers) Rules, 2020, proposing tighter timelines within which distribution licensees must provide new connections and restore supply after outages, along with enhanced automatic compensation payable to consumers for missed Standards of Performance benchmarks, open for stakeholder comments before finalisation.

case: Battery Energy Storage System (Viability Gap Funding) Scheme — Phase II Guidelines
court: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
headline: Phase II Guidelines Issued for Viability Gap Funding to Standalone Battery Storage Projects
summary: The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy has issued Phase II guidelines under the Battery Energy Storage System viability gap funding scheme, revising eligibility criteria for standalone storage capacity procured through competitive bidding and clarifying disbursement milestones tied to commissioning and a minimum operational availability period following commercial operation.

case: National Green Hydrogen Mission — Revised Compliance and Certification Framework
court: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
headline: Revised Green Hydrogen Certification Framework Notified Under the National Green Hydrogen Mission
summary: The Ministry has notified a revised certification framework for green hydrogen production under the National Green Hydrogen Mission, tightening the renewable-energy-sourcing verification standard a producer must meet to qualify output as 'green' hydrogen for incentive purposes, and introducing a standardised third-party certification and audit process producers must complete before claiming production-linked incentiv

case: Carbon Credit Trading Scheme — Compliance Mechanism Sectoral Rollout
court: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
headline: Sectoral Rollout Timeline Notified for Compliance Obligations Under the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme
summary: The Ministry has notified a phased sectoral rollout timeline for compliance obligations under the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS), bringing designated energy-intensive sectors, including thermal power generation above a specified capacity threshold, within the scheme's greenhouse gas emission intensity targets on a staggered basis, with non-compliant obligated entities required to purchase carbon credit certifica

case: Revised E-Auction Rules for Minor Mineral (Sand) Mining Blocks
court: State Directorate of Mines and Geology
headline: State Notifies Revised E-Auction Rules for Sand Mining Blocks, Tightening Bid-Security Forfeiture Conditions
summary: A state Directorate of Mines and Geology has notified revised e-auction rules for minor mineral (sand) mining blocks, tightening the conditions under which a successful bidder's earnest money and bid security can be forfeited for delay in executing the mining lease deed or in commencing operations within the prescribed period, and introducing a shorter cure period before forfeiture takes effect.

case: Suo Motu Proceedings on Distribution Licensee Debt Restructuring Compliance
headline: SERC Initiates Suo Motu Review of Discom Compliance With Debt Restructuring Scheme Milestones
summary: A State Electricity Regulatory Commission has initiated suo motu proceedings to review the concerned state distribution licensee's compliance with loss-reduction and operational-efficiency milestones tied to its participation in the central government's power sector debt restructuring scheme, seeking a detailed compliance report and proposing periodic public disclosure of progress against the agreed milestones.

case: Revised Norms for Computation of Royalty and Dead Rent on Major Minerals
headline: Ministry Notifies Revised Norms for Computing Dead Rent Payable by Mining Lessees During Non-Working Periods
summary: The Ministry of Mines has notified revised norms for computing dead rent payable by a mining lessee during periods when the mine is not in active production, adjusting the applicable rate slabs and clarifying that dead rent remains payable notwithstanding a lessee's claim of force majeure, save in the limited circumstances the revised norms specifically recognise.

case: Revised Guidelines on Forest Clearance Applications for Mining Projects
court: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
headline: Revised Guidelines Streamline Forest Clearance Applications for Mining Projects Below a Specified Forest-Area Threshold
summary: The Ministry has issued revised guidelines streamlining the forest clearance process under the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 for mining projects involving diversion of forest land below a specified area threshold, introducing a consolidated single-window application format and a defined outer timeline for stage-I (in-principle) approval, while retaining the existing, more detailed scrutiny process for larger forest

case: SEBI Circular on InvIT Related-Party Transaction Disclosure for Infrastructure Trusts
headline: SEBI Tightens Related-Party Transaction Disclosure Norms for Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs)
summary: SEBI issued a circular tightening related-party transaction disclosure and unit-holder approval thresholds for Infrastructure Investment Trusts, requiring more granular reporting of transactions between an InvIT and its sponsor group entities, particularly for asset acquisitions and O&M contracts awarded to sponsor-affiliated entities.

case: In re: Infrastructure Debt Fund NBFC — Nirmaan IDF Ltd. (Regulatory Reference)
headline: An Infrastructure Debt Fund NBFC's Exposure Norms Cannot Be Breached Even to Complete a Distressed Project Refinancing
summary: Considering a reference on an Infrastructure Debt Fund NBFC's proposed refinancing of a distressed toll road project, the tribunal noted that RBI's IDF-NBFC exposure and concentration norms are binding ceilings that cannot be departed from even where a refinancing is otherwise commercially sound, directing the IDF to restructure the proposed exposure through a consortium approach instead.

case: Amendment to Insecticides Rules, 1971 — Revised Registration Data Requirements
headline: Insecticides Rules Amended to Require Enhanced Residue and Efficacy Data for New Pesticide Registrations
summary: The Central Insecticides Board and Registration Committee has notified amendments to the Insecticides Rules, 1971 requiring applicants seeking registration of new pesticide formulations to submit enhanced residue-persistence and comparative efficacy data before provisional registration is granted, tightening the evidentiary bar for new agrochemical entrants.

case: Stock Limit Order — Notified Pulses, 2026
headline: Fresh Stock Limits Notified on Traders and Wholesalers of Notified Pulses Under the Essential Commodities Act
summary: The Department of Consumer Affairs has notified fresh stock-holding limits on wholesalers, retailers and big chain retailers dealing in specified pulses under Section 3 of the Essential Commodities Act, 1955, citing price volatility, with states directed to enforce declaration and periodic stock-reporting obligations.

case: APEDA Circular on Organic Export Certification — NPOP Traceability Norms
headline: APEDA Tightens Traceability Documentation for Organic Produce Exports Under the National Programme for Organic Production
summary: The Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority has issued a circular tightening farm-to-consignment traceability documentation required for organic produce export certification under the National Programme for Organic Production, requiring exporters to maintain a continuous, auditable chain of custody records from the certified farm to the export consignment.

case: Circular on e-NAM Licence Suspension for Repeated Quality-Grading Disputes
court: e-NAM Grievance Cell / State APMC Appellate Authority
headline: State APMC Appellate Authority Clarifies Procedure Before Suspending a Trader's e-NAM Licence Over Quality-Grading Complaints
summary: A state APMC appellate authority has issued clarificatory directions requiring that a trader's e-NAM (electronic National Agriculture Market) trading licence not be suspended over repeated farmer complaints about produce quality-grading without first affording the trader a recorded opportunity to respond to each specific complaint before the concerned market committee.

case: Opposition Proceedings — Regional Produce GI Application
headline: GI Registry Rejects Opposition to Regional Basmati-Adjacent Rice Variety's GI Application, Cites Distinct Agro-Climatic Registration Criteria
summary: The Geographical Indications Registry has rejected an opposition filed against a regional rice-growers' association's application to register a geographical indication for a distinct aromatic rice variety, holding that the opponent failed to establish that the variety's registered agro-climatic growing area and its established quality attributes overlapped with an already-registered GI for a separate variety.

case: NABARD Circular on FPO Governance and Fund Utilisation Reporting
headline: NABARD Tightens Quarterly Fund-Utilisation Reporting Norms for FPOs Availing Equity Grant Support
summary: NABARD has issued a circular tightening quarterly fund-utilisation and governance reporting requirements for Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs) that have availed equity grant support under the central FPO promotion scheme, requiring board-approved utilisation certificates and disclosure of related-party transactions with member-directors.

case: Revised Minimum Wage Notification — Agricultural and Allied Farm Labour
headline: State Labour Commissioner Notifies Revised Minimum Wages for Agricultural and Migrant Farm Labour, With Seasonal Piece-Rate Schedule
summary: The state Labour Commissioner has notified revised minimum wage rates for agricultural and allied farm labour under the Minimum Wages Act, 1948, including a separate seasonal piece-rate schedule applicable to harvest-time migrant labour engaged through labour contractors.

case: Circular on Poultry Farm Biosecurity Licensing Under State Livestock Regulations
court: State Animal Husbandry Department Appellate Authority
headline: Appellate Authority Clarifies Documentary Requirements for Renewal of Poultry Farm Biosecurity Licence
summary: A state animal husbandry appellate authority has issued a clarificatory order on the documentary requirements for renewal of a commercial poultry farm's biosecurity licence under state livestock regulations, holding that a renewal cannot be withheld solely for a delay in filing the biosecurity self-audit report where the farm has otherwise maintained continuous compliance records.

case: Land Acquisition Compensation & Reversion Jurisprudence
headline: Unutilised Acquired Land Must Be Returned Proportionately — Eminent Domain Is Not an Indefinite Land Bank
summary: Across a series of 2025–2026 rulings, the Supreme Court has held that the State's power of eminent domain must be exercised fairly and strictly for the stated public purpose, that compensation must reflect the highest bona fide comparable sale exemplar rather than a diluted averaging method, and that agricultural land acquired but left unutilised for a public purpose must, in appropriate cases, be returned proportion

case: Committee Report on BNSS 144
headline: Section 125 CrPC Applications Pending on 1 July 2024 Continue Seamlessly as Section 144 BNSS Proceedings
summary: Clarifying the transition from the Code of Criminal Procedure to the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, courts have held that maintenance applications filed under Section 125 CrPC before the BNSS came into force continue to be maintainable and are treated as proceedings under the corresponding Section 144 BNSS, without requiring parties to refile.

case: Central Adoption Resource Authority
headline: CARA Streamlines Foster-to-Adopt Timelines for Long-Term Foster Placements
summary: The Central Adoption Resource Authority issued updated guidance streamlining the process by which a child in a long-term, well-settled foster placement can move to a formal adoption under the Hindu Adoption and Maintenance Act or the Juvenile Justice Act framework, aiming to reduce procedural duplication for families already caring for the child.

case: Surrogacy (Regulation) Act Insurance Requirement
headline: Insurance Regulator Clarifies Minimum Medical Insurance Coverage Required for a Surrogate Mother
summary: Following queries from registered surrogacy clinics, the insurance regulator issued clarificatory guidance on the minimum medical insurance coverage that must be procured for a surrogate mother for the duration of the pregnancy and a defined post-partum period, as required under the Surrogacy (Regulation) Act, 2021.

case: Grandparents' Visitation Reference
headline: Grandparents' Visitation Applications Should Be Heard on an Expedited Basis Where Both Parents Are Deceased
summary: In a batch of matters concerning grandparents seeking visitation after the death of both parents of a minor child, the Court directed that such applications be listed and heard on an expedited basis, given the child's need for continuity of family relationships and the grandparents' comparatively limited window to maintain that bond.

case: Maintenance Tribunal Procedure Reference
headline: Summary Procedure Under the Senior Citizens Maintenance Act Upheld Against a Challenge for Denial of Full Trial
summary: Rejecting a challenge that the summary procedure under the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007 denies a fair opportunity to contest a maintenance claim, the Court upheld the Tribunal's streamlined procedure, holding that the Act's object of providing swift relief to elderly parents justifies a summary process, subject to basic principles of natural justice being observed.
